overview.title: Add optional loud greeting mode
overview.intent: Give callers of the greeter a way to emphasize the greeting (e.g. for shouting/emphasis use cases) without changing the default behavior for existing callers.
overview.context: The greeter previously exposed a single `greet(name)` function that always returned a fixed-case greeting string. There was no way to alter the tone/emphasis of the output, and no test coverage existed for the module yet.
overview.summary: The change adds an optional `loud` parameter to the `greet` function. When `loud` is true, the returned greeting is upper-cased; the default (`loud=False`) preserves the original behavior exactly, so existing callers are unaffected. A new test file is added to verify the loud path produces the expected upper-cased output.
attention_points: Only the loud=True path is tested; there's no explicit test asserting default/loud=False behavior is unchanged, though it's a simple enough change that this is low risk.

The parameter is a plain boolean flag rather than e.g. an enum/style option — reasonable for a two-state greeting but worth confirming it matches how the caller intends to expose this (e.g. CLI flag, API param).

steps.title: Add loud parameter to greet()
steps.explanation: This is the actual feature: `greet` gains an optional `loud` keyword argument defaulting to `False`. The greeting message is built first and conditionally upper-cased, keeping the change minimal and backward compatible — no existing call site needs to change.

files.note: Adds `loud` param and conditional `.upper()` transform; default preserves prior behavior.

attention_points: Verify no other module relies on `greet`'s exact prior signature/behavior in a way that a new optional kwarg could break (unlikely, but worth a quick check for positional-arg callers passing extra args).

steps.title: Add test for loud greeting
steps.explanation: A new test file exercises the new `loud=True` path, asserting the greeting is fully upper-cased. This is the first test file for the greeter module, so it also establishes basic test scaffolding (direct import from `src.greeter`).

files.note: New file; single test covering the loud=True case.

attention_points: Consider whether a companion test for the default (loud=False) case should be added for completeness, though the implementation is simple enough that this is optional.
